messages:
Nora: quick thread — we need a lightweight compatibility governance for API migrations. too many one-off shims lately.
Theo: agreed. suggest a tiny lifecycle: proposal -> cataloged-shim -> staged -> retired. each shim needs owner + expiry.
Ravi: add a required test artifact: a pair of example requests (old and new) and expected responses. CI should run them whenever shim changes.
Claire: runtime concerns: shims must be explicit opt-ins per-tenant unless it's a critical security fix. opt-in header example: `X-Rw-Shim-OptIn: SHIM-2026-005`.
Nora: opt-out-by-default is safer. console can let tenants enable for N% traffic.
Theo: header for visibility too: `X-Rw-Shim: id=SHIM-2026-005;status=applied;expires=2026-10-01`. that helps support and telemetry.
Ravi: implementation note: prefer declarative transform rules stored in a small JSON DSL, not ad-hoc JS. sample DSL lines:
```
user.name -> account.display_name [copy]
items[].price_cents -> items[].price_usd [scale:0.01]
```
Claire: require a compat-grade label (stable/heuristic/temp). stable shims can live longer and appear in docs.
Nora: we also need cost-accounting: mark shims that route to a compatibility pool with `billing_tag` so infra costs map to owners.
Theo: monitoring: track `shim_hit_pct`, `shim_latency_p95`, `shim_error_rate`. add alert if hit_pct > 20% after staged rollout or error_rate increase > 2x.
Ravi: add a smoke-check: sample requests run through both shimmed and unshimmed paths; diff outputs; fail staging if diffs exceed threshold.
Claire: runbook: 1) create shim entry + owner 2) add tests and DSL 3) stage to 1-5% tenants 4) monitor metrics for 48h 5) expand or rollback. include rollback triggers and contact.
Nora: on SDKs, we'll emit `shim_applied` events with `shim_id` and `dep_id`. SDK teams should add a deprecation warning hook so apps can log and fix.
Theo: automation idea: when a shim expires, auto-open a ticket for owner and disable shim after 7 days if no action. for long-lived shims require quarterly review.
Ravi: keep shim transforms minimal — no business logic, only shape/field mapping and unit conversions. complex logic belongs in a migration service.
Claire: security check: every shim must list data sensitivity flag. gateway will block shims that escalate data exposure.
deploy-bot: system: catalog entry created SHIM-2026-005 by Nora at 1769987682. staging rollout enabled for 2% tenants.
Nora: action items: Theo to draft catalog API (ETA 3d), Ravi to author test harness and smoke-check (ETA 4d), Claire to update gateway to surface headers and enforce TTLs (ETA 1w). I'll write the short runbook and add checklist to the architecture board (ETA 2d).
Theo: noted. we'll reconvene after the staging window.
Claire: no objections. closing.
